items.title: Pro-Trump deniers crash against 'blue tsunami'
items.summary: Political pundits had anticipated a wave of legal challenges from election deniers seeking to contest the results of Tuesday's vote, or efforts by Trump himself to tilt the outcome in his favour — as he did when he tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat. "Election day 2026 featured a few rumours about election integrity. "Absent a political elite to champion election denialism, rumouring about election integrity has not coalesced into a coherent or significant narrative to explain election results."

items.title: Zahid: Malaysia-Türkiye US$10 billion trade target "achievable"
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Malaysia and Turkiye's trade target of US$10 billion by 2030 is achievable, especially through the procurement of defence and security equipment. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the balance of trade between both countries is currently in Malaysia's favour. "From the effort of both countries, the target is achievable, especially from Malaysia, in procuring defence and security equipment," he said.

items.title: The high price of corruption in private sector
items.summary: The case clearly sends a clear message that company directors must carry out their functions and use their given authority in the company's interests, and not for personal benefit. Under Section 218 of Companies Act 2016, directors and company officers who misuse their positions to benefit themselves or others, or to harm the company, may face up to five years in prison, a fine of up to RM3 million, or both. Under Section 213 of the Companies Act 2016, directors must act honestly, make decisions for proper reasons and put the company's interests first.

items.title: Anwar open to foreign workers for oil palm harvesting, with mechanisation pledge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is open to approving foreign workers for oil palm harvesting, provided the plantation industry commits to reducing its reliance on migrant labour through mechanisation. He also said any abuse of workers, including foreign workers, must be met with firm action. Speaking at the 14th Malaysia Madani Scholars Forum today, Anwar was responding to a question from a plantation industry representative who said most planters had yet to receive their foreign worker quotas for this year.

items.title: Zahid, Erdogan discuss Malaysia-Türkiye ties, trade expansion
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi paid a courtesy call on Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan today. The discussion also covered raising the bilateral trade target from US$5.6 billion in 2025 to US$10 billion by 2030. Zahid also congratulated Turkiye on becoming Asean's 12th Dialogue Partner.

items.title: Penang police probe viral video alleging patrol officers' misconduct
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Police have launched an investigation into a viral video alleging misconduct by patrol officers during an enforcement operation at Puncak Erskine in Tanjung Tokong. Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police became aware of the footage circulating on social media today. Rozak said police were investigating the allegations under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

items.title: Landslide closes Jalan Rawang-Kuala Selangor in Gombak
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Jalan Rawang-Kuala Selangor (B27) at Section 9.90 in Gombak has been closed to all vehicles following a landslide that damaged part of the road structure last night. The Selangor Public Works Department (PWD) said the landslide also brought down trees, blocking the entire road. "This caused slope instability and soil movement, resulting in the collapse and damage to part of the road structure," it said.

items.title: BSN customers may face difficulties withdrawing cash at other banks' ATMs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) customers may experience difficulties withdrawing cash from automated teller machines (ATMs) operated by other banks through the Malaysian Electronic Payment System (MEPS). BSN said the disruption was due to high ATM transaction volumes. It advised customers to use their BSN ATM cards at BSN machines temporarily.

items.title: NST Leader: Avoiding the traps that turn Malaysians into drug mules
items.summary: Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah has told the Dewan Rakyat that drug-trafficking syndicates are targeting young people, including students and graduates, with irresistible financial and material incentives. These syndicates must know their targets are particularly susceptible to inducements for what may appear to be harmless and routine tasks as human couriers. Parents, universities and educational institutions must be particularly on the lookout and be proactive in educating young people about these syndicates' recruitment practices.

items.title: Malaysia hits 40th in global governance index, PM warns against complacency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's rise to 40th place among 133 countries in the Chandler Good Government Index (CGGI) 2026 reflects the government's continued efforts to strengthen national administrative capacity, integrity and effectiveness, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the government's priority remained building robust institutions, improving public service delivery and ensuring every development effort brought tangible benefits to the people. Malaysia climbed two places from 42nd in 2025 in the index, which evaluates national governance performance across seven core pillars.

items.title: Deepavali decorations bring Kota Baru family closer
items.summary: The 51-year-old said decorating the house ahead of the Festival of Lights was a simple yet meaningful family tradition that brought his loved ones closer. Assisted by his two sons, M. Sai Siddhart, 19, and Kavin, 13, as well as their cousin R. Hareetaran, 36, Murugaih said the preparations also provided an opportunity for family members to spend quality time together. He said about 30 siblings and other relatives would usually gather at his mother's house to celebrate the festival.

items.title: Malaysia has 6 months' rice supply, 8 months' fish stock amid cyberwar threat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has enough rice to last at least six months and fish for eight months should a cyberattack disrupt the country's communication networks, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. Order food supplies?" he said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Najib remains in Kajang Prison as house arrest transfer stalls, lawyers confirm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak remains in Kajang Prison despite preparations for his transfer to house arrest, his lawyers confirmed tonight. The lawyers maintained that all conditions imposed under Najib's conditional royal pardon had been fulfilled following the payment of his RM50 million fine earlier today. Under the first, payment would settle only the fine, with Najib continuing to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

items.title: [UPDATED] Najib's lawyers accuse A-GC of disregarding King's order, demand immediate house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyers have accused the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) of disregarding the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's order by delaying his transfer to house arrest. Messrs Shafee and Co demanded that Najib be transferred immediately to his Taman Duta residence, maintaining that the conditions imposed under his conditional royal pardon had been fulfilled. They maintained that any legal questions surrounding the High Court's orders should be referred to the court rather than used to delay Najib's transfer.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 6, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: A-GC seeks Najib stay The Attorney-General's Chambers has called for Najib Razak's house arrest to be temporarily suspended pending legal clarification of his conditional royal pardon. Loke resigns as minister Transport Minister Anthony Loke has resigned with immediate effect, citing DAP's objection to Najib serving the rest of his sentence under house arrest. Anwar disagrees with Umno Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says he disagrees with Umno paying Najib's RM50 million fine, but respects the party's decision.

items.title: [UPDATED] 'Illogical' to keep Najib in Kajang after home gazetted as prison, say lawyers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyers have questioned the Attorney-General's Chambers' (A-GC) move to delay his house arrest when his Taman Duta residence has already been gazetted as a prison. It moves him from one gazetted prison to another, as His Majesty has ordered," they said. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur, to be a prison under Section 3 of the Prison Act 1995.

items.title: Najib's Taman Duta residence gazetted as prison
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's residence in Taman Duta here has been gazetted as a prison under the Prisons Act 1995. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta. The development follows Umno's payment of Najib's RM50 million fine earlier today, fulfilling a key condition of the royal pardon that allows him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.

items.title: Tech stocks suffer bloodbath as US midterms fuel AI fears
items.summary: The Tokyo and Seoul stock markets closed out their weeks with losses of six per cent following the Nasdaq's 5.5 per cent collapse on Thursday, its worst showing since April last year when Trump unveiled his wide-ranging global tariffs. The London, Paris and Frankfurt stock markets shed around two per cent nearing the halfway stage despite featuring few technology firms. Tokyo dived six per cent Friday as Japanese tech investor SoftBank gave back more than 10 per cent, while chipmaker Kioxia collapsed 8.7 per cent and semiconductor tester Advantest retreated five per cent.

items.title: Brent oil price benchmark set for biggest weekly drop since 2020
items.summary: LONDON: Oil prices were set for a sharp weekly fall after the election losses of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party raised hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran and a stock market sell-off, though attacks on vessels in the Middle East continue to provide a floor to crude. In a whiplash see-saw session on Friday, Brent crude futures for January were up 31 cents, or 0.3 per cent, to US$98.60 a barrel by 1129 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures edged up by 48 cents, or 0.5 per cent, to US$91.00.

items.title: UAE shares fall as geopolitical uncertainty keeps traders cautious
items.summary: Abu Dhabi's benchmark index dropped 1.3 per cent to hit an 18-month low, weighed down by a 1.7 per cent fall in real estate giant Aldar Properties. Top lender Emirates NBD fell 1.3 per cent, while toll operator Salik Company slipped 1.1 per cent. Emaar Properties' shares closed 0.2 per cent lower.

items.title: Asyraf: Delaying Najib's house arrest would defy King's decree
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki has warned that any attempt to delay former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest would amount to defiance of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's decree. https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/1572295/updated-najibs-house-arrest-should-be-suspended-pending-legal-review His remarks came after the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) said the implementation of Najib's house arrest should be temporarily deferred pending clarification of legal issues surrounding his conditional royal pardon. The A-GC said Najib's detention status should remain unchanged pending further legal clarification.

items.title: British Airways owner sees profits hit by soaring jet fuel costs
items.summary: International Airlines Group (IAG) said pre-tax profits fell 12.9 per cent to €1.63 billion in the three months to Sept 30, while operating profits slumped 15.9 per cent to €1.73 billion. It said a 4.5 per cent rise in revenues was not enough to offset a 30.4 per cent jump in jet fuel costs, as well as disruption caused by Air Traffic Control outages. IAG said its total fuel costs are expected to soar to €8.9 billion for the financial year, even with actions to fix prices in advance.

items.title: Sterling dips as stock rout boosts dollar, outweighs rate rise boost
items.summary: LONDON: The pound fell against the dollar on Friday, as a stock market selloff hit currencies more geared towards global growth, while holding broadly steady against the euro around a 19-month high. "The market impact of yesterday's Bank of England (BoE) policy update was overshadowed by the deepening selloff for AI-related investments," said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG. "The pound has recently been supported by growing optimism over stronger UK growth, higher UK yields and fiscal concerns becoming a bigger market issue in the euro area than in the UK," said Hardman.

items.title: Najib house arrest: Police remove cordon near his residence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have removed the cordon at the Jalan Langgak Duta junction near Datuk Seri Najib Razak's residence this evening. The statement came hours after Umno settled Najib's RM50 million fine and the High Court issued an Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine, directing his immediate release while requiring him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028. Under the first interpretation, payment of the RM50 million fine would satisfy only the fine component of Najib's sentence, while his prison term would remain in force until Aug 23, 2028.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Friday, Nov 6, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? [[nid:1572389]] KUALA LUMPUR – Members of the media wait outside the residence of former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak in Langgak Duta. NSTP/AZIAH AZMEE [[nid:1572386]] KUALA SELANGOR – Members of the Saujana Utama Volunteer Fire Brigade carry out cleaning work around Masjid At-Taufiqiah in Bandar Seri Coalfields following recent flooding.

items.title: MARC downgraded Zetrix AI's RM2bil IMTN to DIS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has downgraded Zetrix AI Bhd's RM2 billion Islamic Medium-Term Notes Programme to a default rating of DIS after the company failed to settle an outstanding RM25 million payment due today. In a statement, the rating agency said the downgrade followed its earlier decision to lower Zetrix AI's rating to CIS on Oct 30. "Accordingly, MARC Ratings will no longer provide analytical coverage on Zetrix AI," it said.

items.title: Health Ministry fills 11,969 posts this year, remaining positions to be filled by 2027
items.summary: MOH, in a statement today, said the remaining 6,671 posts, or 35.79 per cent, are in the process of being filled, with 2,418 officers expected to complete their application, appointment and placement procedures this year. “Of the remainder, 4,253 officers will only be placed next year, including 3,061 officers who will be appointed by the Public Service Commission (SPA) this year but placed early next year. According to MOH, the 11,969 successfully filled positions involved the appointment process by SPA and the subsequent placement of officers at relevant health facilities.

items.title: Families of 54 Malaysians killed in Nepal-Tibet floods to receive RM10,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of the 54 Malaysians who died in the Nepal-Tibet flood tragedy on Aug 26 will receive a one-off payment of RM10,000 each through the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma). Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the decision was made by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim following detailed discussions at today's cabinet meeting. Ramanan said he had directed Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra) director-general K. Raveendran Nair to obtain detailed information from the Finance Ministry and contact the victims' next of kin soon.

items.title: Ramanan: RM10,000 one-off aid for families of all 54 Malaysian flood victims in Nepal-Tibet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — All families of the 54 Malaysian victims of the Nepal-Tibet flood tragedy on August 26 will receive a one-off payment of RM10,000 through the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma). Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the matter was decided by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim after detailed discussions at today’s Cabinet meeting. “We discussed it at length in the Cabinet, and the Prime Minister decided that a one-off payment of RM10,000 will be given to each victim’s family, but they must follow the list set out under Nadma.

items.title: Hektar REIT cancels EGM on RM125mil KYS KL East International School acquisition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hektar Real Estate Investment Trust (Hektar REIT) has announced the cancellation of its upcoming unitholders' extraordinary general meeting (EGM), which was originally scheduled for Nov 16. The cancelled meeting was called to seek unitholders' approval for the proposed acquisition of leasehold interest in part of a land in Setapak, together with the existing buildings and a new one to be constructed there, comprising of an international and private school known as KYS KL East International School from KYS College Sdn Bhd (KCSB). Following an assessment, the REIT manager's board noted that certain conditions precedent remain outstanding.

items.title: Najib returns to Kajang Prison after HKL medical check-up
items.summary: KAJANG: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who underwent a medical examination at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) this evening, returned to Kajang Prison here tonight. Najib, 73, was earlier reported to have undergone a medical examination at HKL after the vehicle carrying him was seen leaving the Kajang Prison complex this evening. Najib was reported to have settled the RM50 million fine imposed on him in the SRC International Sdn Bhd funds misappropriation case today.

items.title: Najib returns to Kajang Prison after AGC calls for house arrest deferment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A vehicle believed to be carrying former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returned to Kajang Prison tonight, hours after his earlier departure had sparked expectations that he would be transferred to house arrest. Najib, 73, had left Kajang Prison at about 2.37pm accompanied by several escort vehicles, shortly after his lawyers delivered a High Court order allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. However, the AGC subsequently announced that the implementation of the house arrest arrangement should be temporarily postponed pending legal clarification over the conditional royal pardon granted to Najib and the effect of the court order.

items.title: Bank Negara takes action against two entities over unapproved advertising of foreign currency services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia has taken enforcement action against Najmuldin Exchanger and Nusantara Global Network over suspected contraventions of the Financial Services Act 2013 (FSA). The action relates to the advertising of foreign currency buying and selling activities without the central bank's written approval. "The enforcement action was undertaken by Bank Negara with the assistance of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), as part of Bank Negara's continuous enforcement efforts to safeguard the public against potential financial risks associated with the unauthorised buying and selling of foreign currency.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN, Perikatan pledge RM30b investments, free water and no quit rent hike in joint manifesto
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 6 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) today launched a joint manifesto for the 16th Melaka state election. State BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the manifesto, themed “Membina Masa Depan Melaka, Memakmurkan Negara”, outlines 113 initiatives focusing on the cost of living, income, housing and the future of families. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said BN had fulfilled up to 97 per cent of the pledges made in its manifesto for the 15th Melaka state election in 2021.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan warns heavy vehicle drivers to check blind spots as Deepavali traffic builds
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 6 — Drivers of heavy vehicles using highways in Negeri Sembilan are reminded to be more mindful of blind spots and to ensure their surroundings are clear before changing lanes, in order to prevent accidents especially during the upcoming Deepavali festive season. Negeri Sembilan Road Transport Department (RTD) director Jasyindar Singh Sihdu said blind spots on heavy vehicles are a frequent cause of accidents, often occurring when drivers fail to check their side mirrors thoroughly, meanwhile, smaller vehicles following too closely also face significant risks. He noted that areas in the state with high concentrations of heavy vehicle traffic include Kilometre 269 and KM 258 of the PLUS Highway, as well as the roads connecting Ulu Bendul–Terachi, Seremban–Tampin, Seremban–Lukut, Batang Benar–Nilai, Gemencheh and the Bahau–Rompin road.

items.title: Terminal Bersepadu Selatan expects 175,000 passengers over Deepavali travel period, up 20pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Terminal Bersepadu Selatan (TBS) is expected to receive approximately 175,000 passengers throughout this year’s Deepavali festive period, a 20 per cent increase compared to the same festive season last year. “We are also asking online ticket agents (OTAs) to send their own personnel to facilitate matters for passengers who purchase tickets through their respective platforms,” he said at a media session with Bernama at TBS here today. Shazwan said TBS also expects a total of 10,000 bus departures and more than 4,000 bus arrivals throughout the period.

items.title: Six MACC strategic communications officers receive IPRM accreditation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Six officers from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) Strategic Communications Division (BKS) have received the Accreditation in Public Relations (APR) award from the Institute of Public Relations Malaysia (IPRM). The MACC said in a statement that all six recipients completed their accreditation requirements, which included passing and executing a public relations (PR) case study or research publication, attending an interview session, and completing documentation. Meanwhile, Information Department (JaPen) director-general Erwin Khairul Ahmad said in the same statement that the IPRM continues to play an important role in strengthening the public relations profession in Malaysia since its establishment in 1962.

items.title: Bright light seen in Malaysian airspace linked to Nasa satellite re-entry, no debris found, says Mosti
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — The Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Mosti), through the Space Authority Division (BPAngkasa), confirmed receiving preliminary information on reports of bright light sightings in Malaysian airspace over several areas on Wednesday night (November 4). In a statement today, Mosti said the sightings were also linked to the re-entry of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration’s (Nasa) Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory satellite. Mosti added that active monitoring is being conducted by BPAngkasa in collaboration with relevant agencies.

items.title: AGC says Najib’s house arrest should be temporarily postponed pending legal clarification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) says the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest should be temporarily postponed pending legal clarification on the interpretation of his conditional pardon and the effect of a High Court order issued today. However, the AGC said two possible interpretations had arisen over whether payment of the fine meant Najib’s prison sentence in the SRC International case remained in force or was considered completed. Under the second interpretation, payment of the fine would allow the pardon to take full effect, meaning the entire sentence for the SRC International case, including the prison term, would be considered completed.

items.title: Najib taken for scheduled dental examination after leaving Kajang Prison, Anthony Loke says
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has yet to return home after leaving Kajang Prison today, as he was taken to a dental clinic for a scheduled examination, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said. Loke, who earlier announced his resignation as transport minister, said he received the information from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. “The Home Minister had informed me that Najib had not yet been allowed to return home.

items.title: Penang committed to sustainable, well-regulated pig farming, says state exco
items.summary: TASEK GELUGOR, Nov 6 — The Penang state government is committed to ensuring that the pig farming industry in the state continues to be managed in an orderly and sustainable manner through more systematic management, close monitoring and effective enforcement of regulations. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said this approach would allow the industry to continue operating and growing in line with legal requirements and standards without compromising environmental sustainability. “The state government has never shied away from acknowledging the pollution caused by improper management of pig farming waste in the past; instead, we have taken corrective measures to ensure the issue is addressed comprehensively.

items.title: Financially vulnerable Malaysians targeted for recruitment as drug mules, police say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Individuals with financial difficulties, especially those from Sarawak and Pahang, have been targeted by international drug smuggling rings to be recruited as drug mules. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the syndicate’s activities were exposed following the arrest of four individuals, including the foreign mastermind, in Brickfields here yesterday. “Two pairs of shoes and 450 grams of cocaine believed destined for two drug mules were also seized,” he said at a media conference here today, adding the the local men were arrested under Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.

items.title: Malaysia declares 69 items National Heritage, from ‘mi kolok’ to Dewan Rakyat mace
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — A total of 69 heritage items have been recognised as National Heritage 2026, including uthappam , mi kolok and kek lapis , popular foods that reflect Malaysia’s cultural diversity, Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said. In a statement marking the Sixth National Heritage Declaration 2026, he said 39 heritage items had been declared to date, while a further 30 would be gazetted later. “The total includes heritage items recognised as part of efforts to preserve and protect the nation’s heritage, covering tangible and intangible heritage as well as recipients of the Living National Heritage Award (WAKOH),” he said.

items.title: OPR stays at 2.75pc as Bank Negara sees no need to tighten monetary policy, says governor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent reflects its assessment that the rate remains consistent with price stability outlook and sustainable economic growth, said Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour. Abdul Rasheed said global growth demonstrated resilience, supported by factors such as the continued expansion of technology-related investments and strong demand associated with the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. He said Malaysia’s economy demonstrated resilience in sustaining growth, with the third-quarter (3Q) advance estimate recording a 5.3 per cent expansion and average growth for the first three quarters reaching 5.6 per cent.

items.title: Transport Minister Anthony Loke resigns as Najib returns home to begin house arrest
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook has announced his resignation after former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak left Kajang Prison to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. Loke said his stance on the matter had not changed and that his resignation would take effect the moment Najib arrives home. “However, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had informed me that Najib had not yet been allowed to return home,” he said.

items.title: Zahid reminds Loke of pledge to resign from Cabinet post if Najib is released for house arrest today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called on Transport Minister Anthony Loke to step down today if former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is released following the settlement of his RM50 million fine. Zahid said Loke must honour his pledge, according to a New Straits Times report. “He must do it immediately if Datuk Seri Najib is released today.”

items.title: MetMalaysia forecasts continuous rain in Kelantan, Terengganu from Sunday to Nov 11
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Continuous rain is expected in several parts of Kelantan and Terengganu from Sunday until Nov 11, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). MetMalaysia director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the affected areas in Kelantan include Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok and Pasir Puteh. In Terengganu, continuous rain is expected to affect Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu, Marang and Hulu Terengganu, he said.

items.title: PM disagrees with Umno’s RM50m fine payment for Najib, but respects legal process
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed disagreement with Umno’s decision to pay the RM50 million fine on behalf of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, stressing that corruption and abuse of power must not be taken lightly in the name of friendship. Anwar said personal ties and goodwill towards Najib should not create the impression that corruption and abuse of power involving billions of ringgit could be overlooked. While we have a sense of friendship with Datuk Seri Najib, it must not give the public the impression that corruption involving billions of ringgit can simply be overlooked.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia assessing impact of US midterm election results, including tariffs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government is examining the short and medium-term impacts across various aspects following political developments in the United States (US), where the Republican Party suffered a defeat in the midterm elections on Tuesday. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the matter was discussed in depth during today’s Cabinet meeting and Malaysia will continue to monitor the situation, including potential implications regarding the implementation of reciprocal tariffs. “…however, our relations with the current administration, the existing government, as well as both incumbent and newly elected members of Congress including the House of Representatives will continue,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Taman Kosas Mosque, near here, today.

items.title: Cabinet approves transfer of scheduled waste management powers to Sarawak under MA63
items.summary: Madani government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the memorandum, submitted by the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), was agreed upon at today’s Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The move, he said, would also prevent overlapping jurisdiction between the federal and Sarawak governments. Fahmi also said the transfer of federal legislative powers in environmental matters to Sabah and Sarawak would be implemented in phases, beginning with scheduled waste management, he added.

items.title: Najib exits Kajang Prison to serve out SRC sentence under house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Malaysia’s former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak left prison on Friday after paying a fine that allows him to serve the rest of his sentence at home, an AFP reporter saw. Najib, 73, was whisked from Kajang Prison in a silver car followed by a convoy of vehicles, according to an AFP reporter at the scene. MORE TO COME

items.title: Teo Nie Ching urges govt agencies to conduct cybersecurity audits amid rising hacking threats
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Nov 6 — All government agencies must conduct cybersecurity audits to identify vulnerabilities in their respective digital systems and infrastructure amid heightened hacking threats linked to developments in international conflicts. Teo said efforts to strengthen cybersecurity should also extend to the private sector, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and associations, particularly those that rely on the internet and store data online. She said all organisations, particularly those operating critical infrastructure such as hospitals and banking systems, should allocate dedicated funds for cybersecurity audits.

items.title: Selangor to review approved projects, tighten flood mitigation requirements in high-risk areas
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR, Nov 6 — The Selangor state government will order a review of previously approved development projects to ensure that flood mitigation systems are implemented in high-risk areas. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari saId this measure is part of the state government’s efforts to reduce flood risks and prevent a recurrence of such incidents in the affected areas. Amirudin added that the state government has also identified several other issues contributing to flooding in areas such as Johan Setia, Parit Mahang, Bukit Kuching, and Bukit Hijau.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan Customs seizes RM2.56m in cigarettes, liquor and smuggled goods
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 6 — The Negeri Sembilan branch of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department crippled smuggling activities in two raids on Oct 26, seizing cigarettes, liquor and other goods with a total value of RM2.56 million, including duties. Its director, Jamal Paiman, said the seizures by the Enforcement Division involved various items worth RM359,271, with duties amounting to RM2.2 million. He said the items seized comprised 3,008,200 sticks of cigarettes of various brands, 2,910.64 litres of liquor, 221 electrical appliances and a packaging machine.

items.title: High Court orders Najib’s house arrest after Umno settles RM50m fine payment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The High Court has issued a house arrest order for Datuk Seri Najib Razak after his RM50 million fine in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case was settled today. Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee, a member of Najib’s legal team, confirmed the payment was made by Umno to the High Court registry this morning, according to The Star . “As of this morning, the RM50 million fine before Najib has been paid by Umno to the High Court,” he said during the press conference.

items.title: Johor Domestic Trade Ministry logs 2,373 offences, RM11.6m in seizures in price control crackdown
items.summary: Johor KPDN director Lilis Saslinda Pornomo said that of this total, 1,774 cases involved offences under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011. She said among the offences were the failure to display clear price tags or price lists for goods or services, selling controlled items above the stipulated maximum price and raising prices or profiteering in an unreasonable manner. Lilis Saslinda said the ministry also detected 54 other offences under the Trademarks Act 2019, the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, the Copyright Act 1987 and the Hire-Purchase Act 1967.

items.title: ‘Payment completed’: Umno settles Najib’s RM50m fine, paving way for house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Umno has completed all payment processes to the Kuala Lumpur High Court for the RM50 million fine imposed on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, the party announced today. “Umno has completed all payment processes to the Kuala Lumpur High Court this morning,” he said. “Umno hereby officially closes the special Najib Razak Solidarity Fund account and no longer needs crowdfunding for this purpose,” he said.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast for six states and Putrajaya until 2pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several areas across six states and the Federal Territory of Putrajaya, expected to last until 2pm today. The warning, issued in a statement at noon today, covers Pahang (Kuantan and Rompin), Selangor (Sepang, Kuala Langat, Klang, Petaling and Kuala Selangor), Putrajaya, and Johor (Kota Tinggi and Mersing). In Sarawak, the affected areas are Mukah (Mukah, Dalat and Matu), Bintulu (Tatau and Bintulu), Sibu, Kapit (Song), Sri Aman (Lubok Antu) and Betong (Betong).

items.title: Najib’s lawyer, special officer enter KL Court Complex as RM50m fine payment speculation mounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A member of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s legal team arrived at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex in Jalan Duta today at noon, according to a New Straits Times report. Lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee was seen entering the complex as speculation grew that the RM50 million fine could be settled, potentially allowing the former prime minister to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest. Lutfi and Farhan were later seen entering the High Court Criminal Registry office together.

items.title: Legal disputes cast doubt on year-end Petronas-Sarawak settlement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A year-end settlement between Sarawak and Petronas is not possible despite Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg expressing confidence that a deal could be reached before the end of the year, a political analyst said. “You cannot get an agreement while these court cases are happening unless Petronas withdraws, or both sides go to the courts and say they want to settle out of court,” Chin said. He had earlier said only administrative and commercial issues remained unresolved.
